title: Adore Beauty Cuts EBITDA Forecast to Between $4 Million and $6.5 Million - Retail News Asia

Adore Beauty Cuts EBITDA Forecast to Between $4 Million and $6.5 Million Skip to content Monday, November 16, 2026 Advertise with us About us Latest Markets Sectors Companies Sector Intelligence The Retail Brief My Retail More Share E-Tailing Adore Beauty Cuts EBITDA Forecast to Between $4 Million and $6.5 Million
 By Aiko Tanaka Australia 2 min read Publication date: Nov 16, 2026 6:11 AM Share | Save korean beauty In this article ( 4 ) In this article
 Supply Chain Snarls Dent First Quarter 
 Margin Squeeze Across Digital Retail 
 Lender Talks and Cash Preservation 
 Prior Volatility Preceded Current Squeeze 
 Adore Beauty Group cut its full-year earnings guidance by roughly half after warehouse commissioning snags dragged revenue down 8 per cent during the first 20 weeks of FY27, ended November 15. Underlying EBITDA is now projected at $4 million to $6.5 million, down from earlier guidance of $9 million to $13 million.
 CEO Sacha Laing pointed to significant disruptions during the go-live and ramp-up of the retailer’s new national distribution centre. Sales dropped 14.1 per cent in the opening 12 weeks of the fiscal year due to severe stock-outs, a challenged service proposition, and necessary adjustments to promotional trading campaigns.
 Trading recovered to a 3 per cent increase over the final eight weeks as the national distribution hub reached full commissioning, but the rebound could not fully offset early fulfillment bottlenecks.
 Supply Chain Snarls Dent First Quarter
 The disruption centred entirely on the go-live and operational ramp-up of the company’s new central fulfillment hub. With stock inaccessible or delayed inside the facility, order fulfillment stalled across core skincare and cosmetics lines.
 Trading recovered slightly once the facility reached full commissioning. Revenue rose 3 per cent year on year over the subsequent eight-week stretch to November 15, yet the rebound failed to erase early losses.
 Margin Squeeze Across Digital Retail
 Consumer spending across discretionary retail remains constrained by persistent cost-of-living pressures. Category competitors have responded by discounting heavily, driving up digital customer acquisition costs while eroding gross margins.
 For operators, automated distribution shifts carry acute risks when executed ahead of peak holiday trading windows. Transition delays immediately turn planned marketing expenditure into stranded costs because inventory cannot clear the dock.
 Lender Talks and Cash Preservation
 Management withdrew full-year top-line revenue guidance entirely, citing persistent volatility across consumer demand. Executive focus has shifted toward balance-sheet management and cash conservation.
 “We have instigated a number of cashflow-related initiatives to ensure the group can operate successfully within its current facilities. Discussions with our banking partner in respect of covenant compliance are ongoing,” Laing added.
 The company is reviewing spending across discretionary software, marketing outlays, and working capital to preserve headroom under existing loan agreements.
 Prior Volatility Preceded Current Squeeze
 Last year, Adore Beauty generated a 4.3 per cent rise in revenue to $207.3 million, but EBITDA dropped by more than 50 per cent to $3.8 million. Operating cost inflation and heightened promotional discounting had already eaten into margins well before the warehouse migration began.
 Attention now turns to whether the fully commissioned warehouse can maintain positive sales growth through the Cyber Week promotional peak and whether lenders grant covenant flexibility before the half-year reporting deadline.
